rule.description: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0.: Ensure ip forwarding is disabled.: Status changed from passed to failed

sca.policy: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0.

check.title: Ensure ip forwarding is disabled.
check.description: The net.ipv4.ip_forward and net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding flags are used to tell the system whether it can forward packets or not.
check.rationale: Setting net.ipv4.ip_forward and net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding to 0 ensures that a system with multiple interfaces (for example, a hard proxy), will never be able to forward packets, and therefore, never serve as a router.
check.remediation: Set the following parameter in /etc/sysctl.conf or a file in /etc/sysctl.d/ ending in .conf: - net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0 Example: # printf '%s\n' "net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0" >> /etc/sysctl.d/60- netipv4_sysctl.conf Run the following script to set the active kernel parameters: #!/usr/bin/env bash { sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0 sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 } - IF - IPv6 is enabled on the system: Set the following parameter in /etc/sysctl.conf or a file in /etc/sysctl.d/ ending in .conf: - net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 0 Example: # printf '%s\n' "net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 0" >> /etc/sysctl.d/60- netipv6_sysctl.conf Run the following script to set the active kernel parameters: #!/usr/bin/env bash { sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=0 sysctl -w net.ipv6.route.flush=1 } Note: If these settings appear in a canonically later file, or later in the same file, these settings will be overwritten.

rule.description: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0.: Ensure password expiration warning days is configured.: Status changed from failed to passed

sca.policy: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0.

check.title: Ensure password expiration warning days is configured.
check.description: The PASS_WARN_AGE parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to notify users that their password will expire in a defined number of days. PASS_WARN_AGE <N> - The number of days warning given before a password expires. A zero means warning is given only upon the day of expiration, a negative value means no warning is given. If not specified, no warning will be provided.
check.rationale: Providing an advance warning that a password will be expiring gives users time to think of a secure password. Users caught unaware may choose a simple password or write it down where it may be discovered.
check.remediation: Edit /etc/login.defs and set PASS_WARN_AGE to a value of 7 or more that follows local site policy: Example: PASS_WARN_AGE 7 Run the following command to modify user parameters for all users with a password set to a minimum warning to 7 or more days that follows local site policy: # chage --warndays <N> <user> Example: # awk -F: '($2~/^\$.+\$/) {if($6 < 7)system ("chage --warndays 7 " $1)}' /etc/shadow.

rule.description: CIS Benchmark for Amazon Linux 2023 Benchmark v1.0.0.: Ensure sudo is installed.: Status changed from passed to failed

sca.policy: CIS Benchmark for Amazon Linux 2023 Benchmark v1.0.0.

check.title: Ensure sudo is installed.
check.description: sudo allows a permitted user to execute a command as the superuser or another user, as specified by the security policy. The invoking user's real (not effective) user ID is used to determine the user name with which to query the security policy.
check.rationale: sudo supports a plug-in architecture for security policies and input/output logging. Third parties can develop and distribute their own policy and I/O logging plug-ins to work seamlessly with the sudo front end. The default security policy is sudoers, which is configured via the file /etc/sudoers and any entries in /etc/sudoers.d. The security policy determines what privileges, if any, a user has to run sudo. The policy may require that users authenticate themselves with a password or another authentication mechanism. If authentication is required, sudo will exit if the user's password is not entered within a configurable time limit. This limit is policy-specific.
check.remediation: Run the following command to install sudo # dnf install sudo.
